newsitem.title: USA: Second home of murdered Colorado child searched.
newsitem.headline: Second home of murdered Colorado child searched.

text.p: Police investigating the murder of 6-year-old beauty pageant winner JonBenet Ramsey searched a family residence in Michigan, a spokesman said on Monday.

Boulder, Colorado, police spokesman Kelvin McNeill said the search warrant regarding the Michigan home was sealed and officials would have no further comment. The girl's body was found in her family's Boulder house December 26.
The family's second house is in Charlevoix, Michigan, where many wealthy people from Detroit have summer homes. It is located on Lake Michigan in the far northern part of the state.
Police on Monday also said they hoped to set up a interview with the girl's parents, but would not label them as suspects.
"There are no named suspects and no arrests pending," McNeill said.
Police submitted written questions to the parents, John and Patricia Ramsey, the couple's spokesman said. "The answers are being prepared," Pat Korten said in a telephone interview.
The parents returned to Colorado on Friday from Georgia, where they had buried the girl. The Ramseys lived in the Atlanta, Georgia, area before moving to Boulder in 1991.

Korten said they "want to be as cooperative (with the police) as is humanly possible." But he said in a case where the parents might still be considered "possible suspects" attorneys have a duty to protect their clients.

The girl's body was found the day after Christmas in her family's 15-room home in a posh neighbourhood of Boulder, 30 miles (50 km) northwest of Denver, about eight hours after her mother phoned police to say she had discovered a ransom note demanding $118,000.
The blond, blue-eyed child was strangled. According to news reports her skull was fractured and she was sexually assaulted, but police remained tight-lipped about aspects of the investigation.
The little girl had been crowned Little Miss Colorado and participated in other beauty contests.
